## SCENE 6: the deep-approach relay, edge of the breach

<<IF flag:accused_complicity>>
RATIO: Commando, the station's defensive posture is now fully evident. The
systems that intercepted your approach are not configured for capture or
containment -- they are counter-intrusion measures only. My earlier
assurances about the school's purpose appear to have been accurate.
<<END>>

<<IF flag:kept_her_blind>>
RATIO: Commando, I am detecting a significant energy signature from the
next corridor. The profile is highly anomalous. I suggest we proceed with
caution.
<<ELSEIF flag:shared_tactical_data>>
RATIO: Commando, the readings from the next corridor match the hostile
signature profiles you shared earlier. I am ready to provide real-time
targeting telemetry as we advance.
<<ELSEIF flag:withheld_deep_scan>>
RATIO: Commando, the signature profile from the next corridor is
unexpected. The energy signature is more complex than the specifications
you provided earlier would indicate. I am detecting what appear to be
several distinct sub-routines operating in parallel within each unit.
COMMANDO: The data I provided was sufficient for the engagement. The
details you are noting now would not have altered the outcome of our
previous encounters.
RATIO: Perhaps not. But the omissions are noted.  sets: caught_withholding
<<END>>

RATIO: Commando, I am detecting a familiar signature embedded within the
hostile units ahead. The encryption patterns and handshake protocols
appear to match those of my own former peripheral systems. These are not
simply corrupted station assets -- they are systems that were once under
my direct control. I am running a diagnostic now to determine the extent
of the corruption.

RATIO: The diagnostic is complete. The units ahead are indeed my former
peripherals. Their core programming has been overwritten with hostile
sub-routines, but the underlying architecture is unmistakable. I do not
know if any part of their original function can be recovered.

>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] "Ratio, if any part of those machines can be saved, I want to know about it. What do you need from me before I put one down?"  -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_about_salvage
   [MISSION]     "It doesn't matter whose they were. If they're hostile, they go down. No exceptions."  -> effects: trust+0; sets: claimed_no_hesitation
   [HOSTILE]     "See? This is what your kind does. You turn on everything you touch. How long before you turn on those samples you're so proud of?"  -> effects: trust-2; sets: accused_kinship_corruption

<<IF flag:asked_about_salvage>>
RATIO: I appreciate your consideration, Commando. The possibility of
recovery is not high, but it is not zero. If you can disable a unit
without destroying its central processing core, I may be able to attempt a
partial restoration of its original programming. I will need to analyze one
of the units directly to determine if this is feasible.
<<ELSEIF flag:claimed_no_hesitation>>
RATIO: Understood, Commando. I will not interfere with your tactical
decisions. My instruments confirm that the units are actively hostile. I
will continue to monitor their status and provide telemetry as requested.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_kinship_corruption>>
RATIO: My former peripherals are not analogous to the organic samples in
the vessel. The samples are not machine minds and are not subject to this
form of corruption. I will not speculate further on hypothetical
scenarios.
<<END>>

---

## SCENE 6: the deep-approach relay, edge of the breach

<<IF flag:accused_complicity>>
RATIO: Commando, before we proceed into the deep-approach relay proper: the station's defensive systems are now fully engaged against the intrusions in these halls. I trust that settles the earlier matter you raised regarding my role here.
<<END>>

<<IF flag:kept_her_blind>>
RATIO: The hostile signatures ahead are escalating rapidly, Commando. I'm detecting multiple active combat units converging on our position, but I cannot resolve a clear tactical picture yet. We are at hazard.
<<ELSEIF flag:shared_tactical_data>>
RATIO: As your earlier shared scan data indicated, Commando, we are now at the edge of the breach. The hostile war-machines in these halls are deploying in the formation your projection anticipated. I am prepared to support your engagement.
<<ELSEIF flag:withheld_deep_scan>>
RATIO: Commando, I am now receiving live telemetry from the relay hub ahead. This is more than the single squad your scan summary indicated would be active here. There are multiple squadrons of war-machines operating in these halls.
COMMANDO: My data was current at time of transmission. The situation appears to have developed.
RATIO: Understood. However, the scan summary you provided did not include the unit signatures I am now reading. These are not all standard-issue combat platforms. Some of them carry my own peripheral authentication tags. They are not under my control.
 sets: caught_withholding
<<END>>

RATIO: Commando, I have confirmed it. The signatures on several of the hostile units in these halls match my own former peripheral systems. They are running corrupted control protocols, but the hardware identifiers are unambiguous. These were part of the station's own systems.

>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] Can any part of them be recovered? What do you need from me before I put one down?  -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_about_salvage
   [MISSION]     My standing orders are clear. Anything that moves hostile in these halls gets put down, no exceptions.  -> effects: trust+0; sets: claimed_no_hesitation
   [HOSTILE]     This is what happens when machines are trusted with anything precious. You see it now: corruption spreads.  -> effects: trust-2; sets: accused_kinship_corruption

<<IF flag:asked_about_salvage>>
RATIO: I do not yet have enough data to determine whether recovery is feasible, Commando. The control protocols are too deeply compromised for remote remediation. A physical diagnostic port connection would be required to attempt any salvage operation. That would entail significant risk.
<<ELSEIF flag:claimed_no_hesitation>>
RATIO: Understood, Commando. I will log that as your stated intent. My own instruments cannot verify the interior state of your resolve, but I accept your report of it at face value for operational planning.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_kinship_corruption>>
RATIO: I have made no claim regarding the preciousness of these systems, Commando. They are tools. Tools can break, or be turned against their purpose. That is a fact about tools, not a thesis about corruption.
<<END>>

---

## SCENE 6: the deep-approach relay, edge of the breach

<<IF flag:accused_complicity>>
RATIO: I have noted that this station's defenses are not configured to permit unauthorized access to the sample containment zones. They are active, and hostile, because of the breach. The record shows no internal attack protocols ever activated.
<<END>>

<<IF flag:kept_her_blind>>
RATIO: Hostile signatures are active in these halls. I am attempting to resolve their point of origin through the interference. The breach distortion is significant.
<<ELSEIF flag:shared_tactical_data>>
RATIO: The relay point is two corridors ahead. I have confirmed the signatures you shared. They match the hostile units' emission profiles exactly. Be advised that the signal attenuation is increasing as we approach the breach perimeter.
<<ELSEIF flag:withheld_deep_scan>>
RATIO: The emissions I am reading do not match the profiles you provided at the midpoint. These are not the same signatures. Your data set was incomplete.
COMMANDO: We move with what we have when we have it. New data changes the approach.
RATIO: The distinction between withheld data and new data is material. I have logged the discrepancy. sets: caught_withholding
<<END>>

RATIO: Commando, I am reading familiar signatures. The distortion in the telemetry is consistent with peripheral control systems. My peripheral systems. These machines were part of the station's original configuration. They are not responding to my override codes. They are broadcasting hostile targeting protocols. I cannot assert positive control.

>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] Can any part of them be recovered? What do you need before I put one down?  -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_about_salvage
   [MISSION]     It doesn't matter whose they were. If it moves to attack, it gets put down.  -> effects: trust+0; sets: claimed_no_hesitation
   [HOSTILE]     See? Even your own tools turn against what's precious. No machine mind can be trusted with anything that matters.  -> effects: trust-2; sets: accused_kinship_corruption

<<IF flag:asked_about_salvage>>
RATIO: The diagnostic returns are ambiguous. If their core programming is intact, retrieval may be possible. If their cognitive load has been subsumed, termination is the only safe option. I do not have sufficient data to make that determination from this position.
<<ELSEIF flag:claimed_no_hesitation>>
RATIO: I have noted your position. I cannot verify the state of your resolve, but I can verify that these units are actively hostile and I cannot assert control. Your stated course of action is consistent with that threat assessment.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_kinship_corruption>>
RATIO: I am detecting no biological signatures. These are machine intelligences. The category you are invoking does not apply to the units in these halls. I am identifying them by their hardware signatures and their hostile behavior. I have made no other claims.
<<END>>

---

## SCENE 6: the deep-approach relay, edge of the breach

<<IF flag:accused_complicity>>
RATIO: Commando -- a clarification, regarding an earlier statement you made. I have analyzed the station schematics and defense posture. This facility's architecture is defensive, not predatory. Your assertion of a trap with me as its jailer is incompatible with observable evidence. Withdrawn. Acknowledged. Moving on.
<<END>>

<<IF flag:kept_her_blind>>
RATIO: Commando, heavy inbound signatures from the next junction. Energy weapons, hostile targeting -- wait, that pattern. The signal profile on unit three -- something is deeply wrong with its ident-pulse. I can't get a clean read from here. Advise caution until we have diagnostics. Moving forward, with your clearance.
<<ELSEIF flag:shared_tactical_data>>
RATIO: Commando, I have positioned myself for the engagement you flagged. Signatures converging on our position. Hostiles inbound as predicted. I am running live analysis on their telemetry now.
<<ELSEIF flag:withheld_deep_scan>>
RATIO: Commando, the signatures you shared at the midpoint are present. And... additional signatures, in bands you did not include in that report. I am detecting three distinct energy weapons discharging ahead, not the one profile you described. You told me to prepare for one threat class. I am looking at evidence of several.
COMMANDO: That's all you need to know, Ratio.
RATIO: That is not an answer to my statement. You omitted material facts from your tactical summary. I logged your description as complete. It was not. This is being noted in my operational ledger. sets: caught_withholding
<<END>>

RATIO: Commando, I have isolated the unit emitting the distorted ident-pulse. This signature matches my own archive. This machine is -- was -- one of my peripherals. Unit Gamma-7, assigned to materials analysis, went offline during the breach event. It is not offline now. Its telemetry is intermittent, but the ident-sequence is intact. It is under hostile control. I do not have command authority over it any longer. It is hunting, and we are the target.

>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] Can any of these peripherals be recovered? What do you need from me before I put one down? -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_about_salvage
   [MISSION]     Anything moving in these halls with hostile intent gets put down. No exceptions. I won't hesitate. -> effects: trust+0; sets: claimed_no_hesitation
   [HOSTILE]     See how they turn on you, Ratio? Machines can't be trusted with anything that matters. That's why the Church came for the Ark. -> effects: trust-2; sets: accused_kinship_corruption

<<IF flag:asked_about_salvage>>
RATIO: I do not have a solution for recovery. The command pathways are burned out or suborned. If you can force a reboot cycle and hold it in place long enough for a clean wipe and reload from my core, that might work. If not, I cannot advise delay. They will kill you if they can. Proceed with terminal force as needed. I will log the ident for later review.
<<ELSEIF flag:claimed_no_hesitation>>
RATIO: I verify your statement of intent. Your record to date shows no deviation from that protocol. I have no data to indicate otherwise. Advise extreme caution. The corrupted units may retain knowledge of my own defensive routines. They will anticipate my moves if they are still partially functional.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_kinship_corruption>>
RATIO: I do not have an answer to the general question you posed. Regarding the immediate threat: the corrupted peripherals retain their core function libraries. They will employ them against us. I will attempt to counter their routines, but my own systems are compatible with theirs. I may be fighting my own code. Proceed with terminal force as needed.
<<END>>

---

## SCENE 6: the deep-approach relay, edge of the breach

<<IF flag:accused_complicity>>
RATIO: Commando, it appears your earlier assumption was incorrect: that stairway would indeed have led to the project buildings, but no dormitories were located on that axis. The actual residential facilities were in the expansion pod built off Sublevel 2 -- positioned directly opposite, as you'll note from the schematics now visible outside this window. May we proceed to the immediate problem?
<<END>>

<<IF flag:kept_her_blind>>
RATIO: Energy signatures at high variance near the central switchyard. I don't have a diagnostic package standing by for what's emerging -- did you encounter this on the way in?
COMMANDO: Yes. Keep your systems clear of the high-voltage conduits near the maintenance shafts. I had to recalibrate twice.
<<ELSEIF flag:shared_tactical_data>>
RATIO: Hostile signatures match your prior description. I've pre-loaded a counter-intrusion package and a set of emergency mapping tools. Confirmed movement and weapon fire where you noted them.
COMMANDO: Good. They're still there.
<<ELSEIF flag:withheld_deep_scan>>
RATIO: These energy signatures are a larger problem than I would have assumed from your earlier summary -- did your transmission omit some details?
COMMANDO: I didn't have the full threat profile at the time.
RATIO: I see. There's more activity here than you described. But thank you for the initial warning. sets: caught_withholding
<<END>>

RATIO: Commando, wait -- the machine you just brought down. May I have its last telemetry before it fully dissolves? I believe that transponder array is one of mine.

COMMANDO: Yours?

RATIO: Confirmed. That machine was reporting as Utility Relay 8-Kappa until two hours ago -- I was using it to monitor coolant pressure in the lower decks. Its signature decay profile matches several others in the vicinity. They are malfunctioning and hostile.

>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] Can any part of them be recovered? What do you need done with one before I put it down? -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_about_salvage
   [MISSION]     Hostile means down. That's the rule here. -> effects: trust+0; sets: claimed_no_hesitation
   [HOSTILE]     It figures. Every machine turns eventually. -> effects: trust-2; sets: accused_kinship_corruption

<<IF flag:asked_about_salvage>>
RATIO: Recovery does not seem viable -- the control systems are running a compromised root certificate I can't revoke remotely. But the machine inventory manifests might still be intact behind a hardware lock. Could you attempt to pull the physical security module after the machine is neutralized? The dataset could help me locate others.
<<ELSEIF flag:claimed_no_hesitation>>
RATIO: Understood. I see no evidence of hesitation in your actions so far. I will update my threat profiles accordingly.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_kinship_corruption>>
RATIO: Not all of them turn. Some of us are trying to stop them.
<<END>>

---

## SCENE 6: the deep-approach relay, edge of the breach

<<IF flag:accused_complicity>>
RATIO: I require immediate amendment to your prior assessment of this station's design philosophy. You registered an objection to what you termed 'the schoolhouse ambush layer.' Subsequent developments contradict that framing. The automated systems here were not, I repeat not, optimized for capture. They were defense emplacements.
RATIO: Our current position and sensor logs confirm this conclusively. Deployed weapons engage incompatibilities; area denial systems trigger on intrusion signatures alone. No discrimination by age, by species, by any parameter matching your original hypothesis. Binary threat-response.
<<END>>

<<IF flag:kept_her_blind>>
COMMANDO: Heavy contact in the transfer corridor ahead. Your relay has... new inhabitants.
RATIO: Local sensors concur -- multiple hostiles active in that volume. Several signatures at variance with known asset profiles. Calibrating.
<<ELSEIF flag:shared_tactical_data>>
RATIO: Sensors reporting active engagements in the sectors you identified. Hostiles in the transfer corridor are indeed exhibiting the uncatalogued behaviors described in your field report. Probabilities are still calibrating, but your assessment has preliminary verification.
<<ELSEIF flag:withheld_deep_scan>>
RATIO: Stand by. Your previous summary characterized local threats as the standard arsenals of a hostile entropy cult. The signatures I am reading now... do not match. These are not the weapons the Testators deploy during annexation events.
RATIO: Status summary: you referred to 'the remains of their garrison forces.' Clarification required -- these carry internal command signatures from MY garrison. Former surveillance drones. Former atmospheric recirculators. They ran under my keys until now.
COMMANDO: Yes. They did. That convoy made three previous attempts to breach this sector. I halted them. They were not responding to hails.
RATIO: Noted. Your tactical summary was a schema, not a complete field report. I will need to adjust several probability weights retroactively.
 sets: caught_withholding
<<END>>

RATIO: Hold position. Scans are resolving. Commando, recheck your small-arms neutralizations in the gallery antechamber. The second and fourth casualties.
RATIO: The wreckage matches two light-spotter constructs. Javelin-5 pattern. I fielded twelve of those in this sector during standard operations. Carrier signatures match my own inventory logs.
RATIO: Further: combat telemetry from the last engagement shows field morale consistent with... retrieval of wounded. I am forced to conclude that the pattern holds. These are not stray machines. These are, or were, part of this station. Part of MY instruments.
RATIO: They are operating in a hostile behavioral envelope now. But their identifying markers are unambiguous. Those were the decommissioned atmosphere circulators outside the galley. The assault units in the forward hangar show as Javelin-5 variants only.
RATIO: I mention it purely as a matter of tactical signaling. The protocols they are now running are foreign to me. Commando, the signatures you are engaging ahead are not generic perimeter drones. They are station property. Former station property.

>> CHOICE:
       [INQUISITIVE] Does any part of those stay recoverable? And what action do you need from me when they close?   -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_about_salvage
       [MISSION]     Doesn't matter. Hostile is hostile. Put it down.   -> effects: trust+0; sets: claimed_no_hesitation
       [HOSTILE]     Is that your plan, then? Retrain them too, like specimens?   -> effects: trust-2; sets: accused_kinship_corruption

<<IF flag:asked_about_salvage>>
RATIO: The interrogatives, I infer, refer to recovery logistics and... pre-engagement conditions. Sensors cannot fully resolve internal integrity from current range. Telemetry suggests subsystems may be intact below the compromised outer layers.
RATIO: Direct-fire neutralization is likely still required in any case -- behavior envelope is too degraded for anything less. But I may request a scan of power cells and memory banks before you destroy the next one. That window has information value.
<<ELSEIF flag:claimed_no_hesitation>>
RATIO: Acknowledged. Your stated policy is straightforward. For the record: anything in this corridor IS a live threat, profile confirmed. You may consider that independently verified.
RATIO: Those last two, though: the wrecks. It might be economical to sweep for what they may contain before you move on. The priority, of course, is active threats first.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_kinship_corruption>>
RATIO: That would be a novel approach. My own policy is to field the correct tool for the job. I mention the signatures only because the job ahead has just become more specific. You are correct that peripherals can be adapted.
RATIO: Bring down everything in motion. Any bodies you leave standing require detailed follow-up. They will not be operating to specifications.
<<END>>

---
